extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students in mathematical logic / number theory
extracted.subtask_description: Formal criteria and constructive procedures for definability, representability, and decidability in weak arithmetical theories (the finitely axiomatized theory AE and its consequences). Covers numeralwise determination, functional representation, closure properties, and connections to computability/Church's thesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantifier elimination / decision procedure for Th NA
rubrics_metrics.description: Existential formulas in the language N≡ (with congruences and inequalities) can be transformed effectively into quantifier-free disjunctions by reducing to a finite search of M consecutive integers (M = lcm of moduli). Thus Th NA (theory of naturals with congruences) admits a decision procedure: check truth of resulting quantifier-free atomic sentences (e.g., n ≡m p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: rewrite formulas to remove equalities and opposite signs, collect lower/upper bounds and congruences, add 0 as a lower bound, compute M = lcm(m0,...,mn−1), and replace ∃x by disjunction asserting one of L_j, L_j+1, ..., L_j+M−1 (and 0..M−1) satisfies the bounds and congruences. Example: an existential formula may convert to a disjunction of 72 conjunctions; atomic checks reduce to congruence/numeral comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of periodic / eventually periodic set
rubrics_metrics.description: A set D ⊆ N is periodic if for some positive p, n ∈ D iff n + p ∈ D for all n. D is eventually periodic if there exist M,p>0 such that for all n > M, n ∈ D iff n + p ∈ D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to characterize definable sets in (N;0,S,<,+): Theorem 32F states that a set is definable in this structure iff it is eventually periodic. Atomic cases yield finite, cofinite, or periodic sets (depending on form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: definability in (N;0,S,<,+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 32F: A set of natural numbers is definable in (N;0,S,<,+) iff it is eventually periodic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To verify definability check eventual periodicity; conversely any eventually periodic set has a quantifier-free definition in N≡ and thus is definable. Atomic formula cases reduce to finite, cofinite, or periodic examples (e.g., nv1 + t ≡m u defines a periodic set of period m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: multiplication not definable in (N;0,S,<,+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary 32G: The binary multiplication relation {(m,n,p) | p = m·n} is not definable in (N;0,S,<,+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: if multiplication were definable, one could define the set of perfect squares, but the squares are not eventually periodic, contradicting Theorem 32F.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE: finite axiom set for subtheory of number theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Set AE consists of eleven specific sentences (S1,S2,L1,L2,L3,A1,A2,M1,M2,E1,E2) formalizing properties of 0, successor S, ordering <, addition, multiplication, and exponentiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These axioms (listed explicitly) are chosen so that N is a model of AE and Cn AE is a finitely axiomatizable subtheory strong enough to represent decidable/recursive relations. Use AE as the base theory for representability results.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE proves quantifier-free truths about N
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 33C: Any quantifier-free sentence τ that is true in N is provable from AE (AE ⊢ τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variable-free terms evaluate to numerals (Sn0) and atomic comparisons reduce to numeral arithmetic congruences; thus AE suffices to deduce any quantifier-free truth of N. Use this to show atomic formulas are numeralwise determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE proves existential truths about N
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary 33D: If an existential sentence τ (∃-sentence with quantifier-free matrix) is true in N then AE ⊢ τ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because witnesses are numerals, convert to quantifier-free true sentence provable in AE, which implies the existential sentence. Note: there exist true universal (∀1) sentences not provable from AE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeralwise determination by AE
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula ϕ(v1,...,vm) is numeralwise determined by AE iff for every m-tuple of natural numbers a1,...,am either AE ⊢ ϕ(Sa10,...,Sam0) or AE ⊢ ¬ϕ(Sa10,...,Sam0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property is used to lift definability-in-N to representability-in-AE. To prove representability in Cn AE, show (i) ρ defines R in N and (ii) ρ is numeralwise determined by AE (Theorem 33E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: representability of a relation in a theory T
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula ρ(v1,...,vm) represents relation R ⊆ N^m in T iff for every a1,...,am: (a1,...,am) ∈ R ⇒ ρ(Sa10,...,Sam0) ∈ T and (a1,...,am) ∉ R ⇒ ¬ρ(Sa10,...,Sam0) ∈ T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently: T proves the instantiated sentence exactly when the tuple is in R. For T = Th N this coincides with definability in N. For Cn AE, one shows numeralwise determination and truth in N to obtain representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion (Theorem 33E) for representability in Cn AE
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula ρ represents a relation R in Cn AE iff (1) ρ is numeralwise determined by AE, and (2) ρ defines R in N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that N is a model of AE: truth in N plus AE proving each instance or its negation yields AE-provability equivalences needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representable in consistent axiomatizable theory ⇒ decidable
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 33F: If R is representable in a consistent axiomatizable theory T (effectively enumerable), then R is decidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision procedure: enumerate sentences of T until either ρ(Sa...) or its negation appears; representability guarantees termination and consistency ensures correctness. Corollary 33G: the same holds for finitely axiomatizable consistent theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: recursive relation
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation R on N is recursive iff it is representable in some consistent finitely axiomatizable theory (in a language with 0 and S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formal notion corresponds (by Church's thesis) to the informal notion of decidability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church's Thesis (informal identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The judgment that a relation is decidable iff it is recursive; i.e., representability in a consistent finitely axiomatizable theory captures the informal notion of decidability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not a theorem but a widely accepted thesis; empirical evidence includes equivalence of many formal models of computation and that all 'intuitively decidable' relations encountered are recursive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and equivalences for computable functions (Theorem 33H)
rubrics_metrics.description: A function f:N^k→N is computable iff there is an effective procedure to produce f(a) from a. Equivalently, when viewed as a (k+1)-ary relation (its graph), f is decidable, and equivalently its graph is effectively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Church's thesis to equate computability with recursiveness. Proof provides constructive procedures to obtain one notion from another (compute then compare; enumerate graph to find value; etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: AE proves finite initial segments of ordering (Lemma 33A)
rubrics_metrics.description: AE proves for fixed k that {x | x < S^{k+1}0} = {0,1,...,Sk0}; in particular AE ⊢ ∀x x < 0 is false (i.e., AE knows small-number facts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful in arguments that use bounded quantification or induction over small numerals; used to show bounded quantifiers are numeralwise determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of variable-free terms in AE (Lemma 33B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any variable-free term t there is a unique natural n such that AE ⊢ t = Sn0, and AE gives effective instructions to find n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures AE can evaluate numerals and is central to showing AE proves quantifier-free truths and to constructing numeralwise determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic formulas are numeralwise determined by AE (Theorem 33I(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every atomic formula (in the language with 0 and S, +, ·, E, <) is numeralwise determined by AE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from theorem that AE proves true quantifier-free sentences; used as base case in closure arguments for numeralwise determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure under Boolean combinations and bounded quantification (Theorem 33I(b),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ and ψ are numeralwise determined by AE then ¬ϕ and ϕ→ψ are numeralwise determined; and if ϕ is numeralwise determined then the bounded formulas ∀x(x<y→ϕ) and ∃x(x<y∧ϕ) are numeralwise determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof for bounded quantifiers uses AE knowledge of finite initial segments (Lemma 33A) and case distinction on existence of a witness; cornerstone for showing many natural relations (like primality) are numeralwise determined and hence representable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional representation of functions in Cn AE
rubrics_metrics.description: A formula ϕ(v1,...,vm+1) functionally represents f:N^m→N in Cn AE iff for every a1,...,am: AE ⊢ ∀vm+1(ϕ(Sa1...Sam0,vm+1) ↔ vm+1 = S^{f(a)}0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stronger notion asserts both existence and uniqueness of the output; the left-to-right half is equivalent to ϕ instantiated at the correct numeral, while the right-to-left enforces uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional representation implies relational representation (Theorem 33J)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ functionally represents f in Cn AE then the same ϕ (viewed as a relation) represents the graph of f in Cn AE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct because functional representation gives AE ⊢ ϕ(Sa0,Sb0) exactly when b = f(a); otherwise AE ⊢ ¬ϕ(Sa0,Sb0).

rubrics_metrics.name: From relational to functional representation (Theorem 33K)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f (as a relation) is representable in Cn AE, one can construct a formula ϕ that functionally represents f by conjoining the representing relation θ(v1,v2) with a uniqueness clause ∀z(z < v2 → ¬θ(v1,z)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction ensures existence (because θ represents f) and enforces minimality/uniqueness using bounded quantification and AE's facts about small numerals; detailed proof shows AE proves the required uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure under composition of representable functions (Theorem 33L)
rubrics_metrics.description: If g is an n-place function and h1,...,hn are m-place functions all representable (functionally), then the composed function f(a) = g(h1(a),...,hn(a)) is representable (functionally) and one can build an explicit representing formula using quantifiers or implications over the representing formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two natural schema: universal form ∀y1∀y2(...→...→ψ(...)) or existential form ∃y1∃y2(...∧...∧ψ(...)); either yields a formula that functional-represents the composition when the components are functional representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure under the μ (least-zero) operator (Theorem 33M)
rubrics_metrics.description: If g(a,b) is representable and for each a there exists b with g(a,b)=0, then the function f(a) = least b such that g(a,b)=0 is representable in Cn AE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent f by the formula ψ(v1,v2,0) ∧ ∀y(y < v2 → ¬ψ(v1,y,0)), where ψ represents g; bounded quantification and numeralwise determination ensure representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantifier-free definability implies representability; closure under Boolean and bounded quantifiers (Catalog item 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any relation having a quantifier-free definition in N is representable in Cn AE. The class of representable relations is closed under union, intersection, complementation, and also under bounded existential/universal transforms of the form 'for some c < b' or 'for all c < b'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Theorem 33I and AE provability of quantifier-free truths. This provides a large base of representable relations including all finite relations and ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of representability of relation and its characteristic function (Catalog item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation R is representable iff its characteristic function K_R is representable (K_R(a)=1 if a∈R, else 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: from K_R one can represent R via ψ(v1,S0); conversely from a formula for R build a formula that functionally represents K_R by distinguishing cases v2=S0 or v2=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images under representable functions preserve representability (Catalog item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is representable and f,g are representable functions, then the set {(a) | (f(a),g(a)) ∈ R} is representable; more generally, applying representable functions to coordinates of a representable relation yields a representable relation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by taking characteristic functions and composing representable functions; allows rearranging and repeating variables in representable relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existentially extended relations by ≤ b are representable (Catalog item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a representable binary relation then P = {(a,b) | ∃c ≤ b: (a,c)∈R} is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use previous closure results and the identity that (a,b)∈P iff (a,Sb)∈Q where Q is existential-with-<' variant; composition with successor yields representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisibility is representable (Catalog item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation 'a divides b' is representable because a|b ⇔ ∃q ≤ b: a·q = b, and a·q = b has a quantifier-free definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalize the existential witness q with bounded quantification and apply closure properties to obtain representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primality is representable (Catalog item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of primes is representable by a numeralwise determined formula: S10 < v1 ∧ ∀x(x < v1 → ∀y(y < v1 → x·y ≠ v1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Theorem 33I (bounded quantification preservation) to assert numeralwise determination; combined with definability in N gives representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pairs of adjacent primes are representable (Catalog item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of pairs (a,b) of adjacent primes is representable by formalizing 'a prime, b prime, a < b, and no prime c with a < c < b' using bounded quantifiers and Boolean connectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Again rely on bounded quantifier closure and AE's knowledge of finite initial segments to obtain numeralwise determination and hence representability.
